subject: Recap: Lumos discovery — monthly tokens, peak TPS & $/1M target
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Roberts <eli@lumos.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Lumos discovery — monthly tokens, peak TPS & $/1M target

Hi Eli —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put a pricing draft in HubSpot:

Summary of what we heard
- Production goal: surface AI assistant for customer support (NLP + summarization + short completion generation).
- Expected steady-state monthly tokens: ~45M tokens/month (primarily inference).
- Peak window: 2–3x traffic spikes during billing cycles, with a peak sustained of ~140 TPS for ~10–15 minutes (99th percentile use-case); typical baseline ~25 TPS.
- Average response size: 350 tokens per call (input+output).
- Target unit economics: Lumos wants to target $10–12 per 1M tokens (target $/1M to evaluate feasibility).

What we need from you
1) Confirm monthly token estimate (45M) or provide a range (min — likely / max — aspirational).
2) Share any expected growth cadence (months to scale to 100M, if applicable).
3) Attach the traffic export you mentioned (CSV is perfect) — I see a placeholder file in the Ops folder; please send so we can validate peak calculations.

Next steps (from our side)
- I’ll put together a price band for Hosted API (tiered by monthly tokens + peak TPS allowance) and three ops scenarios: baseline, burst-tolerant, and committed.
- Karthik will drop in a quick note on burst policy and concurrency-based discounts.
- We’ll add the draft to HubSpot and share a one-pager + sample cost table by EOD Friday.

If those numbers above are off, no problem — just reply with the corrected range.

Thanks again — good conversation; want to make the economics simple for your PM and finance leads.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachments: "lumos-traffic-spreadsheet.csv (text/csv)"
From: Eli Roberts <eli@lumos.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lumos Ops <ops@lumos.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 17:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap: Lumos discovery — monthly tokens, peak TPS & $/1M target

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear notes. Quick confirmations and an attachment (exported from our analytics):

Confirmations
- Monthly tokens: current estimate ~45M tokens/month; conservative range 30M — 60M.
- Peak TPS: we saw historical peaks up to 150 TPS during billing cycles, but 140 TPS sustained for 10–15 minutes is a good planning number.
- Growth: we expect to reach ~80–100M in ~9–12 months if pilot conversion goes well.
- Response size: agree on ~350 tokens average.
- Budget target: Finance is looking at $8–12 per 1M tokens depending on support/SLAs; they asked for a committed vs. on-demand comparison.

Attached: lumos-traffic-spreadsheet.csv (sample week with 1s granularity) — it includes a flagged spike on 2026-04-28.

Can you include in pricing:
- An option that tolerates 2x short bursts (up to 3x) without immediate throttling;
- A committed option that reduces $/1M and includes a small burst reserve;
- Notes on 99th percentile latency SLOs at peak TPS.

Also, Marissa — looping you for any security/compliance items we should prep.

Appreciate it,
Eli
Product Lead, Lumos AI
eli@lumos.ai | +1 (617) 555-0199

Attachment: lumos-traffic-spreadsheet.csv (text/csv)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Eli Roberts <eli@lumos.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Lumos discovery — monthly tokens, peak TPS & $/1M target

Eli / Vanessa —

Thanks for the attachment, Eli — that helps a lot. A couple of clarifying notes from the pricing/ops side: 

1) Pricing bands we’ll draft for you (quick sketch):
   - On-demand (no commit): $13 / 1M tokens, with standard peak throttling policy;
   - Committed (3–12 month): $9 — $11 / 1M tokens depending on committed monthly units and required burst allowance;
   - Dedicated reserved: custom pricing (SLA & burst reserve included).

2) Burst handling options:
   - Short bursts (<=3x for <=15 minutes): we can include a small free-burst buffer in committed tiers (subject to approval);
   - 99th percentile latency: we can target <300ms at baseline TPS; during peak windows we’ll surface a latency vs TPS curve so you can trade cost vs latency.

3) Inputs we still need to finalize the draft table:
   - Confirm committed monthly unit you’d like priced (e.g., 50M vs 75M);
   - Confirm whether Finance prefers a blended $/1M (avg) or a tiered model (cheaper at higher bands).

Action items
- Vanessa: I’ll add the draft price table to the HubSpot deal and set a follow-up for early next week for a quick review call.
- Eli: if you can indicate a preferred committed anchor (50M or 75M) that’ll speed approvals.
- Karthik: will prepare a short note on how our autoscaling/burst policies apply to the CSV sample (I'll include a pointer to the peak window).

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Pricing Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
